[b][i]Hacknet[/i] is an absolutely outstanding hacker-simulator experience.[/b] They really got it right. For what may look like a monotonous and boring text-based experience, this game will get your heart pounding and leave you on the edge of your seat. 

[b]The experience makes you really [i]feel[/i] like a hacker.[/b]

[i]Essentially, this is a sandbox computer world simulator not that different from our own, where you will enter commands and slink around the internet completing quests.[/i] Commands in many cases are nearly identical to IRL commands (particularly thinking of DOS, here). The UI is perfect - especially QoL upgrades like autocomplete, and a great help function really go a long way here. The story and music are awesome, too.

[b]Pros:[/b]
+Excellent hacker experience
+Sandbox-type world where you really feel like you have open-ended control
+Metric tons to do
+You can play this at work and nobody will know any better
+Excellent music
+Outstanding story
+Simple UI, especially if you are used to command-based OS

[b]Cons:[/b]
-Not really any that I can think of; I've even had people that are not computer nerds at all try this and they get hooked just as quickly as I did

[b]Totally worth the experience.[/b] This game really thinks outside the box, and makes you rethink your ideas on what makes a game fun.

Before coming across Hacknet I first played Uplink. A hacking game quite like this one. I thoroughly enjoyed it, and when I came across Hacknet on the store page when it was released I loved the idea of a newer version. Little did I know I was stumbling across potentially one of the best games I have ever played!

Unlike other games, Hacknet's beautiful story is woven into dialogue and .txt files. Some of these are hidden so you feel like the story is being slowly unveiled to you until you finally discover what is happening.

The gameplay is one of the things I quite enjoy about this game. You begin with simple tools allowing you to access lightly secured systems. As the game progresses, you gain more tools and skills until you are hacking your way into complex and difficult systems. This feels quite satisfying to grow from a beginner into a skilled hacker. As you explore the systems in Hacknet, you are encouraged to dig deeply into the systems, often uncovering interesting parts of the story and some rather comical dialogue. The game also puts you on edge, as when you begin you are told you are being tracked and are encouraged to always remember to cover your tracks. This feeling becomes quite exhilarating as you are hacking into secure systems and deleting your tracks with seconds to spare for your own safety.

Overall, this game is unlike Uplink, the game I expected it to be like. And is an amazing gem of a game in it's own way. If you're looking for a game that gives you the experience of hacking, being constantly under threat with great gameplay and a beautiful story. I highly recommend this game.

Absolutely amazing game that provides not only a great storyline but also a very natural learning curve. By the time you reach the end of the game you'll be reacting under pressure that would have made you rage quit at the beginning. The command line mechanics are very immersive and do make you feel as if you are hacking someone else's computer whilst the in-game soundtrack puts you right in the centre of a modern spy thriller. The tension in the game is superb, especially if you make a mistake or are racing against the clock, and this is perfectly reflected in the music.

I also love the semi-realistic way that the game uses ports (with real port numbers and protocols), firewalls and proxies rather than the Hollywood *presses all the buttons without showing you what happens.* The way you then have to browse through files to find / work out passwords or discover systems to work through is very gripping and makes you feel very good when you solve a big complex puzzle. Spoiler: [spoiler]When a rival hacker deletes your interface files and reboots your system, the navigation of the console to locate a replacement is VERY satisfying. 10/10 would systematically delete every file off the other hacker's PC again.[/spoiler]

If you are looking for a hacking game then this is a must buy. I only wish we had more to play :D

Holy Hell this game is better than I could have imagined. I bought it on a whim because I thought the idea seemed interesting but I've been sucked in and played 10 hours already!

While not incredibly long, this game was a lot of fun. As a programmer, the fact that *NIX-like commands are used was both a good and a bad thing. While driving the game purely from the terminal was straightforward, I often found myself typing variants of the comands that the game does not recognize (i.e. 'cd -', 'ls -la', 'rm -rf dir\*.*').

I found that the puzzles were not too hard, but I think if the game were longer it would get quite repetitive. Many have asked if this is like 'real' hacking or that they feel like the are in Mr. Robot. In my experience, 'real' hacking isn't nearly as easy, nor predictable. That said, even though I deal with these kinds of systems professionally, this game was very fun and I think it will give you a taste of the command line.

Bottom Line: Worth $10

On a personnal I would compare to a precursor, uplink.

Hacknet as uplink :
- Keep hacking feeling
- Are beautiful in their style and release period

Hacknet is mostly keyboard (terminal) directed (it would be great if it could be completely with the option do do stuff by mouse) while Uplink is completely mouse directed.

Uplink goes far in the concept of wan and man/lan, teach us more about security, that hardware are part of the hacking process, active and passive trace and the importance of clearing logs.

Hacknet goes more in the command line branch, familiarize you with typing with the possibility to see and compare the effects in the terminal and the graphic interface, It goes more in the concept of taking control by getting access of more services of the target system. Most of the command can be used and looks like regular linux command.

Uplink is CPU driven, programs are slower the more you start them but doesn't consider RAM usage, your filesytem has a size limit and all file (including all programs) need to fit it, you also need to consider free blocks of storage memory.

Hacknet is RAM driven, the limit of programs depends of your memory but doesn't consider CPU usage, you have a directory based filesystem using a tree similar to unix/linux (/home /bin /sys).

I never finished Uplink because of the lack of command line interface, and so I liked Hacknet for that point, but I feel now I need a game that puts me to the next level, one that combine the two parts ...

Final thought : I use linux since 2007 so nearly a decade, I do most things in terminals, for me the game was disapointing when a repetitive task was done by the mouse (sending mails)
Though repetitive at times this game has some absolutely brilliant moments that you won't forget.

Hacknet is without doubt the best storyline game i have played in the last few years, and i cannot say anything else than: BUY IT NOW!

I think of Hacknet as a spiritual successor to Uplink, it has a good blend of fresh ideas and features borrowed from Uplink. When I compare the two, I view Hacknet as the more realistic game, whereas Uplink is more Hollywood styled. 

Hacknet features real Linux/UNIX commands, as well as real port numbers, Port 21 for FTP, Port 22 for SSH, 1433 for SQL etc. Now playing this won't teach you how to hack but it kind of gives you an idea of how it works, each system has a set number of ports that have to be open before you an crack it. Some of the later game systems have Proxy servers and Firewalls. Proxies can be overcome by opening a shell on 3-4 computers and telling them to spam it with junk traffic and data, meaning that it will allow unchecked traffic through, whereas Firewalls take a bit more time, you have to analyse it and doing so will reveal some characters, once you think you've got it you type SOLVE [FIREWALL SOLUTION] and it will check to see if it matches. 

Some tools can be run while a Proxy is up, but not while a Firewall is active and some can't be run with a Proxy active but they work while a Firewall is up. 
Each tool has it's own visual effect while it works and they're all beautifly done. My favorites being PortHack and SQL_Mem_Corrupt. 

The game is a bit more linear compared to Uplink, in Hacknet you're forced into the story as soon as the game begins, whereas with Uplink the story kicks in a couple of weeks into the game after some freelance work.

Hacknet has some intresting things to search for though, certain documents such as IRC logs are pretty funny. 

Overall though I'd say it's worth the buy, espiecally due to it getting a free multiplayer and some DLC content later in the year. And the soundtrack fits the game extremely well.

And for those who are intrested, the font used in the >HACKNET_ title can be found here: http://www.dafont.com/kremlin.font?text=HACKNET
